# The packages the reports were generated with, from reports/linux-freeze.txt,
# which is pip freeze on the reference machine -- now with the hashes that make
# the versions bind.
#
# The versions are unchanged from the ones this file carried before the hashes
# were added. What is new is that they now pin bits rather than names: a bare
# `==` pins no bits at all, because a wheel can be rebuilt and re-uploaded
# under the same version.
#
# What --require-hashes buys, and what it does not. The command below lists
# every distribution file the index offers for each version -- every wheel for
# every platform, and the sdist -- so an install refuses a file that is not one
# of them, which is the failure a bare `==` cannot catch. It does NOT single
# out the one wheel the reference machine installed: any published file of that
# version satisfies the check, including one built for another platform.
# --python-platform narrows the resolution, not the accepted set.
#
# Where the hashes came from. The command is the one this file already
# prescribed, run on a machine with index access rather than on the reference
# machine, which has none; --no-deps because this list is already the whole
# environment and a resolver would add to it. It produced 592 hashes over the
# 30 versions below. The uv that ran it reports 0.12.13, which is not the
# 0.12.3 the Containerfile pins for the image build -- two machines, two
# installs -- and that could not be checked from here.
#
# uv's own record of the command follows. Its --output-file names the file the
# result was written to on that machine, before it was moved into place here.
# This file was autogenerated by uv via the following command:
#    uv pip compile --no-deps --generate-hashes --python-version 3.13.5 --python-platform x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -o requirements-freeze.hashed.txt requirements-freeze.txt
